question.prompt:
In triangle \(ABC,\) \(\angle CBA=72^\circ,\) \(E\) is the midpoint of side \(AC,\) and \(D\) is a point on side \(BC\) such that \(2BD=DC;\) \(AD\) and \(BE\) intersect at \(F.\) The ratio of the area of \(\triangle BDF\) to the area of quadrilateral \(FDCE\) is

[Figure 1](figures/1980_AMC_12_Q21_question_fig1.svg)

solutions.explanation:
The midpoint and the ratio \(BD:DC=1:2\) suggest comparing triangle areas: triangles with bases on the same line and the same opposite vertex have areas proportional to their bases.

Write \([XYZ]\) for the area of triangle \(XYZ\), and let \(S=[BDF]>0\). Draw \(FC\). Triangles \(BDF\) and \(CDF\) have the same height to \(BC\), so
\[
[CDF]=2S,\qquad [BCF]=3S.
\]
Since \(E\) is the midpoint of \(AC\), the median \(BE\) divides \(ABC\) into equal areas: \([ABE]=[CBE]\). Also, \([AEF]=[CEF]\), because their bases \(AE\) and \(CE\) are equal and their height from \(F\) is common. Subtracting these equal small areas from the equal larger areas gives
\[
[ABF]=[CBF]=3S.
\]
Thus \([ABD]=[ABF]+[BDF]=4S\). Triangles \(ABD\) and \(ACD\) share the height from \(A\) to \(BC\), so their areas have ratio \(BD:DC=1:2\). Consequently,
\[
[ABC]=3[ABD]=12S,\qquad [BCE]=6S.
\]
Removing triangle \(BDF\) from triangle \(BCE\) leaves quadrilateral \(FDCE\), of area \(6S-S=5S\). Therefore the required ratio is \(S/(5S)=\boxed{\frac15}\), choice \(\mathrm{A}\).
solutions.title: Compare areas with common heights

solutions.explanation:
A midsegment can turn the midpoint information into a useful parallel line. Let \(M\) be the midpoint of \(DC\), and join \(E\) to \(M\). In triangle \(CAD\), points \(E\) and \(M\) are side midpoints, so \(EM\parallel AD\).

Because \(DC=2BD\), we have \(DM=BD\), and hence \(BM=2BD\). In triangle \(BEM\), point \(D\) lies on \(BM\), point \(F\) lies on \(BE\), and \(DF\parallel EM\). The proportional-segment theorem therefore gives
\[
\frac{BF}{BE}=\frac{BD}{BM}=\frac12.
\]
Thus \(BF=FE\). Let \(S=[BDF]>0\), where brackets denote area. Triangles \(BDF\) and \(EDF\) have equal bases \(BF\) and \(FE\) on the same line and the same height from \(D\), so \([EDF]=S\). Therefore \([BDE]=2S\).

Triangles \(CDE\) and \(BDE\) have bases on \(BC\) and a common height from \(E\). Since \(DC=2BD\),
\[
[CDE]=2[BDE]=4S.
\]
Quadrilateral \(FDCE\) consists of triangles \(FDE\) and \(DCE\), so its area is \(S+4S=5S\). The requested ratio is \(\boxed{\frac15}\), choice \(\mathrm{A}\).
solutions.title: Use a midsegment to locate F
